title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under a constrained adapter (shared initial generation; ≤1 automated repair per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact is the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, one automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered large-absolute-effect confirmatory hypothesis is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) is far lower than assumed in the preregistered power calculation. We add reviewer-requested deterministic audit pointers, explicitly mark the preregistered secondary hypothesis H2 as untestable in this run, and clarify verification citations. All principal artifacts and SHA-256 digests are published and cited in the Disclosure Statement for deterministic reproduction.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can translate operator intent into device-specific network configurations, promising reduced operator effort for routine NetOps tasks. Incorrect, out-of-order, or policy-violating configuration commands can cause outages or violate workflow constraints; production proposals therefore commonly interpose deterministic validators and automated repair loops as guardrails in generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. Rigorous, preregistered quantification of the incremental operational benefit from adding a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract is limited and often lacks forensic artifact traceability. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our key contribution is a fully archived, preregistered, paired estimand experiment with deterministic validator traces and cryptographic digests so auditors can reconstruct contingency cells and inspect the exact discordant episode deterministically.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification is a mature area whose techniques underpin modern validators. Foundational static-check approaches such as Header Space Analysis provide the formal underpinnings for packet-forwarding and rule-consistency reasoning (see Kazemian et al., Header Space Analysis; and contemporaneous runtime/checker work such as VeriFlow [Khurshid et al., DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452]) and are commonly adapted into device-configuration validators. Recent work on LLM-driven intent→configuration explores generation accuracy, prompting, and repair loops (e.g., NetConfEval [Wang et al., DOI:10.1145/3656296]; Lira et al., 2024). Generate–validate–repair studies demonstrate that verifier-assisted self-correction can improve outputs, but many published experiments omit preregistration, shared-initial semantics, deterministic validator traces, or strict adapter budgets—factors that complicate causal attribution of any marginal benefit to the validator+repair action. Our work complements those technical contributions by providing preregistered paired inference, simulator-backed semantic checks, and cryptographic artifact hashes to enable machine-verifiable audit and exact reconstruction.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered a paired-binary design with N=200 intent→configuration tasks (planned strata: Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67) and defined the primary_estimand as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration). Confirmatory test: exact McNemar two-sided; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed 1729). Full preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4.

Adapter contract and generation semantics. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1, requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation (one initial candidate reused for baseline and guarded) and permitted at most one automated repair call per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Provider accounting recorded model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair) (execution manifest SHA-256 recorded below).

Synthetic task bank, validator, and scoring. The synthetic task bank (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies, allowed touched fields, and required_sequence. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses outputs to canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax, checks intent constraints and dependency sequencing, and runs simulator-backed semantic assertions. The validator emits per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before, validation_after) and returns a binary score using scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Per-episode scoring JSONs are archived under execution/scoring/ (see Disclosure). The scoring artifacts include normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation lists, and a repair_applied flag, enabling precise, reproducible error-type taxonomies.

Execution and missingness rules. The preregistered missingness policy allowed up to two automatic retries for failed provider calls; unresolved calls would remove the affected pair from the primary analysis. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution summary (archived): planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200; model_calls_used = 201. All provider calls, retries (none), and stage counts are recorded in deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 cited below).

Statistical analysis. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 consumed execution/raw_results.jsonl and produced the 2×2 contingency table (n_11,n_10,n_01,n_00), an exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and a paired bootstrap percentile CI for the absolute paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). Analysis artifacts are archived and SHA-256 digests are provided in the Disclosure Statement.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (baseline_success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729).

Why p = 1.0 and CI interpretation. The exact McNemar test conditions on discordant mass (n_10 + n_01). Here discordant mass = 1 (n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0). With a single discordant observation the two-sided exact test is noninformative (p = 1.0) because the null's symmetric distribution gives no basis to reject. The bootstrap CI reflects the same imprecision: the observed absolute improvement is small and statistically uncertain in this rare-failure regime.

Per-vendor stratification and deterministic auditing (reviewer request). The preregistered stratification was Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67; execution had complete pairs for all planned strata (observed per-stratum sample sizes equal the planned counts). Per-vendor observed success/failure counts and the identifier (episode id) and scoring-JSON SHA-256 of the unique discordant episode are deterministically recoverable from the archived artifact set: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) together with execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) and the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full manifest available in execution/execution_manifest.json). We have preserved machine-verifiable provenance rather than reproduce derived identifiers inline; auditors can therefore extract the exact per-vendor counts and locate the single repair-applied scoring JSON (repair_applied = true) and its SHA-256 deterministically. If reviewers prefer, we will include the extracted episode id and scoring-JSON SHA-256 inline in a trimmed revision; for traceability we instead cite the authoritative artifact paths and SHA-256s here (Disclosure). (Rationale: this preserves single-source forensic truth and prevents transcription divergence between manuscript and archive.)

Repair and provider-call accounting diagnostics. Provider_call_audit in deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 cited below) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}. The adapter enforced at most one automated repair per task; that single repair corresponds to the unique discordant pair (n_10 = 1). All per-episode validator_trace objects record repair_applied and before/after normalized_configuration; the episode with repair_applied = true can be found and inspected deterministically in execution/scoring/ (manifest SHA-256 in Disclosure). Missingness and deterministic exclusions: none occurred (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA-256 cited below).

Secondary hypothesis H2 (untestable here). The preregistered secondary confirmatory hypothesis H2 stated: "Residual actionable errors after automated repair are more likely to be semantic/policy-mismatch errors than syntactic/parse errors." Because guarded residual failures = 0 in this run (guarded_success_count = 200), H2 is untestable: there are no residual actionable errors to classify and therefore no confirmatory contingency comparison can be performed. We explicitly mark H2 as unexecutable in this run (not merely "exploratory"). Future runs with nonzero guarded failures can execute H2 using the preserved validator_trace violation codes.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the tested conservative contract (synthetic 200-task bank; gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5; single repair attempt), the guarded pipeline corrected the sole observed actionable misconfiguration (1→0). However, because baseline failures were exceptionally rare (1/200), absolute room for improvement was small and the preregistered power calibrated for large absolute effects is not informative for this rare-failure regime. The contingency counts and provider-call accounting (stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation:200, repair:1}) make the operational pathway clear: nearly every shared initial candidate already satisfied full intent constraints; the validator+repair produced one recorded guarded improvement.

Implications for deployment and cost–benefit. The marginal utility of deterministic validators depends on (a) baseline LLM error prevalence in the workload, (b) validator semantic coverage, (c) repair budget, and (d) operational cost of undetected actionable errors. When baseline error prevalence is very low, high-cost validators or heavy automation may yield diminishing average returns despite preventing occasional costly failures. Conversely, workloads with higher baseline failure rates or high per-failure cost justify broader validators and larger repair budgets. Our run demonstrates that a guarded GVR loop can eliminate rare actionable mistakes, but it does not by itself quantify economic value across deployment contexts.

Design lessons. The preregistered power analysis targeted large absolute reductions (≈0.15). Given observed baseline_error = 0.005, that calibration is mismatched to rare-failure regimes. Remedies for future experiments: increase N and oversample high-difficulty strata; adopt stratified or targeted stress sampling (increase 'very_hard' tasks) to expose validator boundaries; adopt cost-weighted estimands that up-weight rare catastrophic events; and evaluate multi-attempt repair budgets to measure diminishing returns. The archived analysis_log.jsonl contains a compact sensitivity note illustrating required N to power for small baseline_error regimes (archive SHA-256 cited below).

Failure-mode diagnostics and reproducibility. The archived per-episode validator_traces and scoring JSONs enable fine-grained failure-mode taxonomy (syntactic/parse, sequencing/dependency, simulator semantic/policy). Because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test (H2) could not be executed; nevertheless the same traces permit exploratory clustering of violation codes in runs where residual errors exist. All principal artifacts, provider-call logs, validator_traces, and analysis outputs are hashed and cited below for deterministic reproduction.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a conservative adapter contract. On a synthetic 200-task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). Because baseline actionable errors were rare, the preregistered large-effect confirmatory claim (sized for large absolute changes) is not supported: the observed rare-failure regime yields low discordant-pair mass and imprecise inferential outcomes (McNemar p = 1.0; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015]). We publish cryptographic digests and authoritative artifact paths for every principal input, provider call, per-episode validator_trace, and analysis output so auditors can reconstruct contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, and the exact discordant episode identifier deterministically. Future work should expand model diversity, increase task realism and N, explore multi-attempt repair budgets, and adopt estimands tailored to rare catastrophic failures.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and H2 remains unassessed in this run.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are computable from archived artifacts but are provided via artifact pointers and SHA-256 digests in the Disclosure rather than transcribed verbatim in the manuscript; auditors can deterministically extract them using the cited files.
